title: Enlarging a solution modulo q^n to contain a power of a unit
statement: Let $k$, $\Lambda$, $\mathfrak q$, $n$, $\varphi:k[y_1,\dots,y_m]\to\Lambda$, $\mathfrak p=\varphi^{-1}(\mathfrak q)$, $P=k[y_1,\dots,y_m]_{\mathfrak p}$ and $P/\mathfrak p^nP\to D\to\bar\Lambda:=\Lambda_{\mathfrak q}/\mathfrak q^n\Lambda_{\mathfrak q}$ be as in the conclusion of [lem-weil-pbc-popescu-solution-modulo]: $k$ a field of characteristic $p>0$, $\Lambda$ Noetherian [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring] and geometrically regular over $k$ [def-weil-pbc-g-ring], $\mathfrak q\Lambda_{\mathfrak q}=\mathfrak p\Lambda_{\mathfrak q}$, $P\to\Lambda_{\mathfrak q}$ flat [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map], and $P/\mathfrak p^nP\to D\to\bar\Lambda$ local homomorphisms of local Artinian rings with the first essentially smooth [def-weil-pbc-essentially-smooth-ring-map] and the second flat. Then for every $\lambda\in\Lambda\setminus\mathfrak q$ there are an integer $q>0$ and a factorization $D\to D'\to\bar\Lambda$ of $D\to\bar\Lambda$ by local homomorphisms of local Artinian rings such that $D\to D'$ is essentially smooth, $D'\to\bar\Lambda$ is flat, and the image of $\lambda^q$ in $\bar\Lambda$ lies in the image of $D'$.

source.place: Smoothing Ring Maps, Lemma Tag 07FI (lemma-enlarge-solution-modulo, line 2624), Section 07FF

proof.text: (Setup.) Write $\bar\Lambda=\Lambda_{\mathfrak q}/\mathfrak q^n\Lambda_{\mathfrak q}$, $\psi:D\to\bar\Lambda$ for the given flat local homomorphism, $\mathfrak m_D$ and $F=D/\mathfrak m_D$ for the maximal ideal and residue field of $D$. $\Lambda_{\mathfrak q}$ is local with maximal ideal $\mathfrak q\Lambda_{\mathfrak q}$ and residue field $\kappa(\mathfrak q)$ [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime], so $\bar\Lambda$ is local with maximal ideal $\mathfrak m_{\bar\Lambda}=\mathfrak q\bar\Lambda$, $\mathfrak m_{\bar\Lambda}^n=0$, and residue field $\kappa(\mathfrak q)$. Since $\psi$ is local it induces a field homomorphism $F\to\kappa(\mathfrak q)$, through which we regard $F\subseteq\kappa(\mathfrak q)$ (Stacks: $k\subset F\subset\kappa(\mathfrak q)$). $\bar\Lambda$ is a $k$-algebra, so $p\cdot1=0$ in $\bar\Lambda$. Let $\bar\lambda$ be the image of $\lambda$ in $\bar\Lambda$ and $\alpha\in\kappa(\mathfrak q)$ the image of $\lambda$; $\alpha\neq0$ as $\lambda\notin\mathfrak q$. By [lem-weil-pbc-artinian-local-noetherian-nilpotent] $D$ and $\bar\Lambda$ are Noetherian and $\mathfrak m_D$ is nilpotent; by [lem-weil-pbc-artinian-local-unique-prime] their only primes are their maximal ideals. Exactly one of three cases occurs: $\alpha\in F$; $\alpha$ algebraic over $F$ but not in $F$; $\alpha$ transcendental over $F$ (not a root of a nonzero polynomial over $F$ [def-weil-algebraic-element]).

source.place: Smoothing Ring Maps, proof of Lemma Tag 07FI (lemma-enlarge-solution-modulo, lines 2642-2675)

proof.text: (Claim, the first part of the Stacks argument.) Let $D_1$ be a local ring with residue field $F_1$ and $\psi_1:D_1\to\bar\Lambda$ a local homomorphism, and let $\mu\in\bar\Lambda$ have residue $\mu_0\in\kappa(\mathfrak q)$ with $\mu_0\neq0$ and $\mu_0$ in the image of $F_1\to\kappa(\mathfrak q)$. Then $\mu^{q}\in\psi_1(D_1)$ for every power $q=p^e$ of $p$ with $q\ge n$. Proof: choose $x\in D_1$ whose residue maps to $\mu_0^{-1}$; then $x\notin\mathfrak m_{D_1}$, so $x$ is a unit of $D_1$, and $\varepsilon=\psi_1(x)\mu-1$ has residue $0$, i.e. $\varepsilon\in\mathfrak m_{\bar\Lambda}$ (Stacks: $x\bar\lambda=1\bmod\mathfrak q$). As $p=0$ in $\bar\Lambda$, $(a+b)^p=a^p+b^p$, hence by induction on $e$ $(1+\varepsilon)^{p^e}=1+\varepsilon^{p^e}$, and $\varepsilon^{q}\in\mathfrak m_{\bar\Lambda}^{q}\subseteq\mathfrak m_{\bar\Lambda}^n=0$. So $(\psi_1(x)\mu)^q=1$ and $\mu^q=\psi_1(x)^{-q}=\psi_1(x^{-q})\in\psi_1(D_1)$. (Stacks says '$q$ divisible by $p$'; what is needed is a $p$-power $q\ge n$.)

source.place: Smoothing Ring Maps, proof of Lemma Tag 07FI (lemma-enlarge-solution-modulo, lines 2642-2675)

proof.text: (Case $\alpha\in F$.) Take $D'=D$ with the identity $D\to D$ and $D'\to\bar\Lambda$ equal to $\psi$ (flat by hypothesis). The identity is $D\to D[y_1,\dots,y_0]=D$, smooth by [lem-weil-pbc-polynomial-ring-smooth] with $n=0$, hence essentially smooth (take $P=D$, $S=\{1\}$ in [def-weil-pbc-essentially-smooth-ring-map]). By the Claim (step 2) with $D_1=D$, $\mu=\bar\lambda$, $\mu_0=\alpha$, the image of $\lambda^q$ lies in $\psi(D)$ for $q=p^e\ge n$.

source.place: Smoothing Ring Maps, proof of Lemma Tag 07FI (lemma-enlarge-solution-modulo, lines 2642-2675)

proof.text: (Case $\alpha$ transcendental: $D[\bar\lambda]$ is a polynomial algebra over $D$; Stacks: 'this works because $D[\bar\lambda]$ is in fact a polynomial algebra over $D$ in this case', written out.) Let $\theta:D[t]\to\bar\Lambda$ be the $D$-algebra map $t\mapsto\bar\lambda$. The $F$-vector space $V=\bar\Lambda/\mathfrak m_D\bar\Lambda$ maps $F$-linearly onto $\kappa(\mathfrak q)$ (as $\mathfrak m_D\bar\Lambda\subseteq\mathfrak m_{\bar\Lambda}$), sending the class $v_i$ of $\bar\lambda^i$ to $\alpha^i$; the $\alpha^i$ ($i\ge0$) are $F$-linearly independent because $\alpha$ is transcendental over $F$, hence so are the $v_i$. Extend $(v_i)_{i\ge0}$ to an $F$-basis $(v_i)_{i\ge0}\cup(w_\beta)_{\beta\in B}$ of $V$ and lift each $w_\beta$ to $\bar\Lambda$. $D$ is local with nilpotent maximal ideal (step 1) and $\bar\Lambda$ is a flat $D$-module, so by [lem-weil-pbc-local-artinian-basis-when-flat] the family $(\bar\lambda^i)_{i\ge0}$ together with the lifts is a $D$-basis of $\bar\Lambda$. In particular the $\bar\lambda^i$ are $D$-linearly independent, i.e. $\theta$ is injective: $D[\bar\lambda]=\theta(D[t])\cong D[t]$.

source.place: Smoothing Ring Maps, proof of Lemma Tag 07FI (lemma-enlarge-solution-modulo, lines 2642-2675)

proof.text: (Case $\alpha$ transcendental: the ring $D'$.) Let $\mathfrak m=\theta^{-1}(\mathfrak m_{\bar\Lambda})$ (Stacks: $\mathfrak m=D[\bar\lambda]\cap\mathfrak q\bar\Lambda$). Since $\psi$ is local, $\mathfrak m_D[t]\subseteq\mathfrak m$, and modulo $\mathfrak m_D[t]$ the map $D[t]\to\kappa(\mathfrak q)$ is $F[t]\to\kappa(\mathfrak q)$, $t\mapsto\alpha$, which is injective as $\alpha$ is transcendental; hence $\mathfrak m=\mathfrak m_D[t]$, a prime ideal ($D[t]/\mathfrak m=F[t]$ is a domain). Set $D'=D[t]_{\mathfrak m}$ [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime] (Stacks: $D'=(D[\bar\lambda])_{\mathfrak m}$, the same ring by step 4). $D[t]$ is Noetherian [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra-noetherian] and so is $D'$ [lem-weil-pbc-localization-noetherian]; $D'$ is local with maximal ideal $\mathfrak mD'=\mathfrak m_DD'$, which is nilpotent because $\mathfrak m_D$ is (step 1), so $D'$ is an Artinian local ring by [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-local-quotient-artinian-local] (with $K=0$); its residue field is $D'/\mathfrak m_DD'=F[t]_{(0)}=F(t)$. $D\to D[t]$ is smooth [lem-weil-pbc-polynomial-ring-smooth], so $D\to D'$, a localization of it, is essentially smooth [def-weil-pbc-essentially-smooth-ring-map], and it is local ($\mathfrak m_D\mapsto\mathfrak m_DD'$). Every $s\in D[t]\setminus\mathfrak m$ has $\theta(s)\notin\mathfrak m_{\bar\Lambda}$, a unit of the local ring $\bar\Lambda$, so $\theta$ extends uniquely to $\psi':D'\to\bar\Lambda$ [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime]; $\psi'$ is local ($\psi'^{-1}(\mathfrak m_{\bar\Lambda})=\mathfrak mD'$), its composite with $D\to D'$ is $\psi$, and $\psi'(t/1)=\bar\lambda$.

source.place: Smoothing Ring Maps, proof of Lemma Tag 07FI (lemma-enlarge-solution-modulo, lines 2642-2675)

proof.text: (Case $\alpha$ transcendental: flatness and conclusion.) Apply [lem-weil-pbc-criterion-flatness-fibre-noetherian] to $R=D$, $S=D'$, $S'=M=\bar\Lambda$: these are Noetherian local rings (steps 1 and 5) and $D\to D'\to\bar\Lambda$ are local homomorphisms; $M$ is finitely generated (by $1$) and nonzero over $\bar\Lambda$; $M/\mathfrak m_DM$ is a module over the field $D'/\mathfrak m_DD'=F(t)$, hence free and so flat [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map]; $M$ is flat over $D$ by hypothesis. Hence $\psi':D'\to\bar\Lambda$ is flat. With $q=1$, $\bar\lambda=\psi'(t/1)$ lies in the image of $D'$.

source.place: Smoothing Ring Maps, proof of Lemma Tag 07FI (lemma-enlarge-solution-modulo, lines 2642-2675)

proof.text: (Case $\alpha$ algebraic: a $p$-power making $\alpha$ separable; Stacks cites Fields, Section 'algebraic' (Tag 037H, a label no longer in fields.tex).) $F(\alpha)/F$ is algebraic, so by [lem-weil-pbc-separable-first-purely-inseparable] there is $e\ge0$ with $\beta:=\alpha^q$, $q=p^e$, separable over $F$ [def-weil-pbc-separable-algebraic-extension]; let $\bar g\in F[T]$ be its minimal polynomial, separable and irreducible, so $F(\beta)\cong F[T]/(\bar g)$ is a finite field extension of $F$ inside $\kappa(\mathfrak q)$. The elements of $F(\beta)$ separable over $F$ form a subfield containing $F$ and $\beta$ [lem-weil-pbc-separable-first-purely-inseparable], so $F(\beta)/F$ is finite and separable algebraic; hence $\operatorname{Spec}F(\beta)\to\operatorname{Spec}F$ is etale [lem-weil-pbc-finite-separable-extension-etale], i.e. $F(\beta)$ is a finite etale $F$-algebra.

source.place: Smoothing Ring Maps, proof of Lemma Tag 07FI (lemma-enlarge-solution-modulo, lines 2642-2675); Fields, Lemma Tag 030K (lemma-separable-first) proof and Lemma Tag 09H0 (lemma-irreducible-polynomials)

proof.text: (Case $\alpha$ algebraic: the finite etale extension $D\to D'$.) $D$ and $\bar\Lambda$ are local rings whose only prime is the maximal ideal (step 1), hence henselian [lem-weil-pbc-local-dimension-zero-henselian] (Stacks: Algebra, Lemma 06RS). By the essential surjectivity in [lem-weil-pbc-henselian-finite-etale-equivalence] (Stacks: Algebra, Lemma 04GK) applied to $D$ and the finite etale $F$-algebra $F(\beta)$ (step 7) there is a finite etale $D$-algebra $D'$ with an $F$-algebra isomorphism $D'/\mathfrak m_DD'\cong F(\beta)$. $D'$ is a finite $D$-algebra, hence of finite type and Noetherian [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra-noetherian]; $\mathfrak m_DD'$ is nilpotent (step 1) and $D'/\mathfrak m_DD'$ is a field, so every element outside $\mathfrak m_DD'$ is a unit modulo a nilpotent ideal, hence a unit: $D'$ is local with maximal ideal $\mathfrak m_DD'$, residue field $F(\beta)$, and Artinian [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-local-quotient-artinian-local] (with $K=0$). $D\to D'$ is local, and it is etale, hence essentially smooth [def-weil-pbc-essentially-smooth-ring-map] (remark (a) there).

source.place: Smoothing Ring Maps, proof of Lemma Tag 07FI (lemma-enlarge-solution-modulo, lines 2642-2675)

proof.text: (Case $\alpha$ algebraic: the factorization $D'\to\bar\Lambda$; Stacks: 'since $\bar\Lambda$ is henselian and $F(\alpha^q)$ is contained in its residue field we can find a factorization', written out.) Let $B=D'\otimes_D\bar\Lambda$; $\bar\Lambda\to B$ is etale [lem-weil-pbc-etale-ring-base-change]. Its fibre is $B/\mathfrak m_{\bar\Lambda}B=D'\otimes_D\kappa(\mathfrak q)=(D'/\mathfrak m_DD')\otimes_F\kappa(\mathfrak q)\cong F(\beta)\otimes_F\kappa(\mathfrak q)\cong\kappa(\mathfrak q)[T]/(\bar g)$, and $\bar g(\alpha^q)=0$ in $\kappa(\mathfrak q)$, so $T\mapsto\alpha^q$ gives a surjective $\kappa(\mathfrak q)$-algebra map $\pi:B\to\kappa(\mathfrak q)$, $b\otimes1\mapsto$ (image of $b$ in $F(\beta)\subseteq\kappa(\mathfrak q)$). Its kernel $\mathfrak q'$ is a prime of $B$ over $\mathfrak m_{\bar\Lambda}$ with $\kappa(\mathfrak q)\to\kappa(\mathfrak q')$ an isomorphism. As $\bar\Lambda$ is henselian (step 8), [lem-weil-pbc-henselian-etale-retraction] gives a $\bar\Lambda$-algebra map $\sigma:B\to\bar\Lambda$ with $\sigma^{-1}(\mathfrak m_{\bar\Lambda})=\mathfrak q'$. Put $\psi'(b)=\sigma(b\otimes1)$, $\psi':D'\to\bar\Lambda$. For $d\in D$, $\psi'(d)=\sigma(1\otimes\psi(d))=\psi(d)$: $\psi'$ factors $\psi$. Reducing $\sigma$ modulo $\mathfrak m_{\bar\Lambda}$ gives a $\kappa(\mathfrak q)$-algebra map $B/\mathfrak q'\to\kappa(\mathfrak q)$, necessarily the inverse of the isomorphism induced by $\pi$; so $\psi'(b)\bmod\mathfrak m_{\bar\Lambda}=\pi(b\otimes1)$, and the residue field $F(\beta)$ of $D'$ maps onto $F(\beta)=F(\alpha^q)\subseteq\kappa(\mathfrak q)$; in particular $\alpha^q$ is in its image. $\psi'^{-1}(\mathfrak m_{\bar\Lambda})$ is a prime of $D'$, hence $\mathfrak m_DD'$ [lem-weil-pbc-artinian-local-unique-prime]: $\psi'$ is local.

source.place: Smoothing Ring Maps, proof of Lemma Tag 07FI (lemma-enlarge-solution-modulo, lines 2642-2675)

proof.text: (Case $\alpha$ algebraic: flatness and conclusion.) As in step 6, [lem-weil-pbc-criterion-flatness-fibre-noetherian] applied to $D\to D'\to\bar\Lambda$ and $M=\bar\Lambda$ (Noetherian local rings and local maps by steps 1, 8, 9; $M/\mathfrak m_DM$ is a module over the field $D'/\mathfrak m_DD'\cong F(\beta)$, hence flat [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map]; $M$ flat over $D$) shows that $\psi'$ is flat. Now apply the Claim (step 2) to $D_1=D'$, $\psi_1=\psi'$ and $\mu=\bar\lambda^q$, whose residue $\alpha^q\neq0$ lies in the image of the residue field of $D'$ (step 9): $(\bar\lambda^q)^{q'}\in\psi'(D')$ for a $p$-power $q'\ge n$. So the integer $qq'>0$ and the factorization $D\to D'\to\bar\Lambda$ (step 8: $D\to D'$ essentially smooth; $D'\to\bar\Lambda$ flat) satisfy the lemma. Together with steps 3 and 6 this covers all three cases of step 1.
